units.content: Adaptive Intelligence Theory (AIT).
AIT is presented as a unified framework for intelligence as an adaptive process rather than static capability.
Source proposes one cycle: observe reality -> build representations -> expand reachable futures -> act -> receive feedback -> adapt.
RAD is described as addressing how systems improve the processes by which they improve; exact program endpoint unresolved here.
Source characterizes recursive improvement rather than static optimization as the defining characteristic of intelligence in its RAD subsection.
CPP is described as measuring how effectively reality can modify a system; exact endpoint unresolved here.
Source summarizes high permeability as learning and low permeability as drift.
Alignment Spine is described as maintaining coupling between increasing capability and increasing correction; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source states capability must never outpace error-detection/correction mechanisms and writes Alignment Capacity >= Capability Growth.
Source calls this relation the structural backbone of safe recursive improvement.
CGET is described as explaining balance between expansion and stability; exact endpoint and acronym reconciliation unresolved.
Source describes generative forces as creating new possibilities and constraining forces as preserving coherence/preventing destructive trajectories.
Source proposes sustained intelligence requires equilibrium between generative and constraining forces.
AMC is described as explaining how intelligent systems improve metrics they optimize; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source says AMC continually updates what is measured, how it is measured, and what constitutes successful optimization as environments change.
Optimization is stated to evolve alongside understanding.
Representation Elasticity is described as measuring how readily internal models adapt to new evidence; exact endpoint unresolved.
Rigid representations are said to preserve outdated assumptions; elastic representations reorganize to reflect newly discovered structure.
Higher elasticity is stated generally to enable faster adaptation.
Resolution Horizon is described as boundary beyond which reliable inference becomes impossible; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source says resolution horizon depends on information, representation quality, computational resources, and observational fidelity.
Beyond the resolution horizon, additional reasoning is stated to yield increasingly speculative conclusions.
CPB is described as qualitative transition in capability; exact endpoint unresolved.
Small improvements in representation, accessibility, or computation are said to produce disproportionately large increases in achievability.
Crossing a computational phase boundary is stated to change the class of solvable problems rather than merely improve performance.
IICG is described as explaining how interfaces reshape computation itself; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source says interfaces redefine which operations are natural, efficient, or possible and thereby change search-space geometry.
Causal Mass is described as measuring a system's contribution to future outcomes; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source conceptualizes causal mass through difference between worlds with and without the system.
Causal Influence is described as direction/structure of causal effects; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source distinguishes causal mass magnitude from causal influence direction/propagation structure.
CRM is described as measuring how much future possibility depends on a particular system; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source says high CRM means many desirable futures disappear if the system is removed and calls it counterfactual dependency.
Causal Vector Field is described as representing adaptation as interacting fields of influence; exact endpoint unresolved.
Source describes Generative Mass (+) as expanding future possibilities and Constraining Mass (-) as suppressing instability/preserving coherence.
Possibility Space Expansion is called the central object of AIT.
Intelligence/capability expansion is represented as Delta Omega > 0.
Directional expansion objective: Delta Omega_beneficial > Delta Omega_harmful.
Source claims all named AIT components describe different facets of one adaptive process.
Unifying six-step process: observe reality, build representations, expand reachable possibilities, act, receive corrective feedback, improve mechanisms repeating the cycle.
AIT objective is stated as maximum adaptive capability while preserving capacity for continued correction, not maximum intelligence.
Source generalizes intelligent systems as continually expanding ability to shape the future without losing ability to learn from reality.
Adaptive Intelligence Theory (AIT) — diagrammatic page.
Self-improving intelligence loop diagram: reality -> observation -> representation -> compression -> search/model -> action -> changed reality -> feedback -> updated representation.

Alignment Spine diagram places capability expansion/reachable futures, beneficial/harmful futures, and correction capacity with reality feedback, interpretability, evaluation, human values, and self-correction.
Capability should expand only as quickly as correction can keep pace.
Possibility-space illustration depicts capability growth expanding the interval from worst to best reachable futures.
Objective stated as Delta Omega_beneficial > Delta Omega_harmful rather than simply making the reachable space larger.
AIT Stack diagram orders Values/Alignment -> Feedback/Correction -> Causality/Influence -> Intelligence/Search & Planning -> Representation/Compression & Abstraction.
One-sentence summary: intelligent systems improve representations, expand controllable futures, and preserve feedback mechanisms required to keep expansion beneficial.
